newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy industrial output still stagnant - Isco study.
newsitem.headline: Italy industrial output still stagnant - Isco study.

text.p: Italian industrial output, stalled since the second half of last year, is still stagnant with a resulting negative impact on jobs and domestic demand but there are some slight signs of an upturn, research body Isco said.
Isco's latest survey of industrialists' expectations showed they saw some glimmer of an improvement in spring.

The report said the negative impact of Italy's tough budget deficit-cutting measures was likely to be counterbalanced by renewed optimism on financial markets as the goals of restoring public finances to health were neared.
The falling inflation trend should also help in leading to a loosening of monetary policy, Isco added.

The possibilities of a recovery in output were linked to an expected upturn in export growth, although indications over domestic demand were not too comforting given prevailing pessimism on the part of consumers, the survey showed.
On the employment front, the jobs market also reflected the effects of the prolonged period of stagnation with the total number of employed falling slightly between October and January, Isco noted.
